posts.topic: DeepSeek drops V4-Pro-0813, undercutting frontier pricing again
posts.script:

posts.topic: YC-backed AI startup offered job interviews for company tattoos, then apologized
posts.script:
A YC-backed AI startup just offered job interviews in exchange for a permanent tattoo — and people actually did it.

LemonLime, a Y Combinator-backed AI automation company, promised instant interviews to anyone who got its logo permanently tattooed on their body. Seven applicants took the deal. After the backlash hit, CEO Jordan Zietz apologized on X, calling it ‘poorly exercised judgement’ and offering to pay for tattoo removal for anyone who wants it gone.

This is what the AI-era hiring market actually looks like right now — desperate enough that a startup thought permanent ink was a reasonable interview filter.

posts.topic: OpenAI's IPO filing could land within weeks
posts.script:
OpenAI's public IPO filing could land within weeks — and it would set up the largest tech listing in history.

The company confidentially filed its S-1 with the SEC back in June, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley steering toward a fall debut. A listing could value OpenAI above one trillion dollars, up from its last private valuation of 852 billion. The revenue behind it: roughly two billion dollars every month — though OpenAI is still unprofitable, losing about a dollar twenty for every dollar it earns.

Once that filing goes public, it's the first real look inside ChatGPT's business — and public-market scrutiny will shape how every AI tool you rely on gets priced.
